text:
Samir Gupta: heads-up — we've been seeing steady p99 latency spikes on inference-pool-2 since ~08:10 UTC. throughput dropped ~18% for a handful of pods.
Chao Li: saw that on the dashboard too. any hardware alarms?
Samir Gupta: started checking logs, there's repeated AER/Xid messages on two hosts (rack7-43 and rack7-46). Not full node OOMs, looks like link retrains.
Arielle: can you paste the dmesg slice?
Samir Gupta: sure — grabbed the last 200 lines from rack7-43, stripped noise:
```
[Aug  5 08:09:58] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
[Aug  5 08:09:58] nvidia: GpuId: 1, Xid (PCIe AER) 33, engine: Copy Engine
[Aug  5 08:10:01] nvlink0: link 1 down, retraining
[Aug  5 08:10:02] nvlink0: link 1 up, negotiated width 16
[Aug  5 08:10:07] nvidia: ECC correctable errors increased: 156 -> 182 in 7s
[Aug  5 08:10:10] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Uncorrected error received: id=0104
[Aug  5 08:10:11] kernel: pci_bus 0000:65: link changed, state 1->0
```
Samir Gupta: pattern is repeated every 10-20s for that window.
Chao Li: Xid 33 usually points to memory copy/engine issues. NVLink flip is suspect. Could be flaky NVLink cable or a card intermittently resetting link.
Leo: routing question — are we failing over to other racks automatically? This is reducing effective capacity for hosted API.
Arielle: autoscaler didn't kick aggressively; our batching pipeliner keeps queues long and p99 suffers. We have headroom in eu-west1-dedicated pool but cross-region adds cost/latency.
infra-bot: incident created INC-2025-2190 (auto) — linked hosts: rack7-43, rack7-46 — severity: medium — sla-impact: partial-threshold breaches on inference-pool-2.
OpsLead: immediate steps: cordon + drain affected nodes, move critical traffic to warm standby pool, open vendor RMA if hardware persists. Who can coordinate drain?
Chao Li: I can run cordon/drain now. plan: tag GPUs as `hw:pending-rma` after drain, avoid scheduling new pods, mark in inventory.
Samir Gupta: suggested commands:
```
kubectl cordon rack7-43
kubectl drain rack7-43 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
# add annotation to node
kubectl annotate node rack7-43 redwood/gpu-status=hw:pending-rma
```
Samir Gupta: also recommend increasing replica set for inference-serving to compensate for ~2 nodes lost: +2 replicas for next 30m. Arielle: can you run that?
Arielle: will scale now. also switching routing policy to prefer dedicated eu-west1 pool for new requests (will increase cost estimate by ~6% for the hour).
Leo: good. capture metrics for before/after so we can show cost vs. SLO impact. put a short note in the incident ticket.
Chao Li: while draining I'll attach `nvidia-smi --query` logs and full dmesg to the ticket. we should also collect NVLink peer stats with `nvidia-smi nvlink --status`
Samir Gupta: vendor next steps: open an RMA for the two cards showing repeated ECC and AER counts. I'll paste the telemetry and request priority because this hits hosted-prod.
infra-bot: RMA ticket RMA-5589 opened with vendor (priority: high). ETA initial response: 48h.
OpsLead: 48h is long. mitigation options in the meantime? firmware/driver update?
Chao Li: safe quick mitigation: set kernel param `pcie_aspm=off` and bump driver to latest minor if not already; also try re-seating NVLink bridge on rack maintenance window. but re-seat requires physical access — ops team can schedule.
Samir Gupta: prefer not to kernel-parameter change across fleet during peak. let's do it only on the affected hosts as a short test if RMA ETA holds.
Arielle: rolling scaling done + routing change applied. monitoring shows p99 dropping back ~9% immediately, still above target but improving.
Leo: action items: 1) Chao cordon+drain + add annotation (in progress). 2) Samir open vendor RMA (done). 3) Ops schedule physical check & potential bridge reseat for rack7 next maintenance window. 4) Arielle increased replicas and routing change (done). 5) Infra to prepare a rollback plan if kernel param change is needed.
Chao Li: cordon/drain completed on rack7-43 at 08:12 UTC, rack7-46 in progress. attaching logs to INC-2025-2190.
Samir Gupta: quick note — ECC counters show mostly correctable errors, not permanent memory faults. vendor may request burn-in logs. capture a 30m window of `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.errors.uncorrectable_single_bit, memory.errors.correctable_single_bit --format=csv` and upload.
Arielle: uploaded post-drain graphs to the incident. cost delta for routing to dedicated pool estimated +$120/hr if traffic stays that way. added to incident notes.
Leo: thanks all. if we still see flaps after reseat + driver upgrade we'll escalate to hardware replacement ASAP. keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
Samir Gupta: I'll post follow-ups after vendor reply or after rack check.
infra-bot: incident updated INC-2025-2190: state=mitigating, assigned=[Chao Li, Samir Gupta, OpsTeam], severity=medium.
Chao Li: one more data point: MSP telemetry shows PCIe AER coalesce count spike correlating with our latency spikes. adding that to the ticket. might be a slot-level power/retimer issue.
OpsLead: noted. setting up a maintenance task for rack7 reseat + BIOS microcode check next Tuesday 03:00-04:00 UTC.
Samir Gupta: perfect. I'll schedule brief post-maintenance smoke test traffic and monitor p99 for 2h.
Arielle: thanks — will keep an eye on cost + SLO dashboards.
Leo: closing loop — if vendor offers a one-off hotfix or microcode, prefer that before RMA swap. but be ready to swap if errors continue.
Samir Gupta: got it. signing off here until next update.
